reviews.text: I really like it. At first, I didn't know how to play, but I gradually explored and was later attracted by the real climbing experience.

In real life, I dare not climb. When I see this new game, I want to give it a try, but I immediately fall in love with it. Each level of this game features a well-known building. It feels like climbing a real building.
This immersive experience is good, but it requires a real VR device to play. If you have a device, you can give it a try

I feel like there's a real need for a fun VR climbing game for PCVR, and was hopeful this might be it, or at least the start of it. Sadly, for now anyway, it isn't. I love the idea, and hope development keeps going and I eventually have to rewrite this review, but for now there are too many frustrations with this game for it to be something I could recommend. Issues I felt it had: - Graphically it's kind of mushy; I feel it could look more impressive than it does. - The grip mechanic is really random and makes no sense whatsoever. Sometimes it grips, other times not. There is no indication of what makes for a working grip (yes, I get the lights on the glove, but when and why does it go red?) - Movement when you're stood free has to be one of the worst implementations I've experienced in a modern VR game. There's no turn. Moving forward will randomly walk you backwards. - On the randomly walking backwards thing: when stood on a flat surface of a building, attempting to move to the wall to carry on can result in you being thrown off and killed for no obvious reason (because of the random backward walk). - When I made it to the top of the first building, nothing happened. There was no indication of what the end-game situation was. - This might just be a me thing, but also I found there was pretty much zero immersion in the game. Something like The Climb 2 *really* made me feel like I was high above the ground and in danger; there was zero sense of that with this. - The music that plays when you're climbing is annoying, far too loud, and can't be turned off. I suspect this might be the immersion-killer now I think about it. If there was the sound of traffic and people below, sounds of the environment around me, the sound of wind blowing past me, I can imagine I'd feel far more immersed. All in all I spent half an hour trying to make it past the very first level and the mechanics of the game seemed to make it impossible at every step. As I say, even when I made it to the top despite those issues, there didn't seem to be a way to actually finish the level. You'd expect the first level to be almost impossible to fail as it will *teach* you the mechanics of the game. I really want to like this. I really would love to see a fun climbing game. Right now, this isn't it. Right now I'd recommend waiting to see how it develops. --- Post update update: I really appreciate the developer responding to what I wrote, and this gives me a lot of hope for this game; I've tried the update and, sadly, I can't honestly change this to a "recommend" at the moment. The sounds are better, and it's great to have the music removed from the climb itself, but other than that all of the main issues remain: - The grip system seems to be a random mystery with no skill needed at all, from what I can tell. - Movement didn't appear to change at all, the way the thumb sticks work seems to ignore any of today's conventions for VR games. - Walking forward and stopping still causes random jump backs, which still throws you off buildings if you're stood on a ledge. - I did finally manage to unlock the second level, and made it to the very top, but the game never registered that I'd made it and it wasn't at all obvious what I was supposed to do to register that I was done.

This is the kind of climbing experience I was waiting on but it has many issues that could be fixed. Falling through structures sometimes, some parts of structures not being grabable. Id like to be able to roam the top when I finish a map and you sort of can but you just clip through the surface except for your head. Would also be cool to have the ability to throw yourself upward when climbing to try and climb higher faster. Overall its some fun and decent views. Came back to downvote because I finally made it to the Eiffel Tower and everytime I load in it spawns me behind an invisble wall I cant get around and wont let me climb it.
The magnificent architecture, climbing into the middle of each building, whether looking up or down, is terrifying. The scene is so realistic, I like it, top! Top!

In addition to having fun, you can also experience the beauty of architecture in various places, killing two birds with one stone, it's great! I especially like games with simple controls. Work is already very tiring, and games are just for relaxation. I don't like games with complex controls
十几个有名的建筑随你心意去攀爬，一个软件等同于十几张门票，而且没有时间空间的限制，超值的软件！有攀登爱好 的人来试试看

Feeling both dangerous and excited, I climbed the Leaning Tower of Pisa, the Statue of Liberty in the United States, the Pyramid of Giza in Egypt, and the Olympic Tower in China. I love this app so much and look forward to playing it again when I have time next time.

The one I most want to climb is the Tower of Harry, starting from the Leaning Tower of Pisa. I have already climbed five or six towers, but this software only unlocks one after climbing one. Otherwise, I would have climbed the Tower of Harry directly to experience the grandeur of this building

I want to see a thousand miles and climb to the next level, so I climbed one tower after another. I truly love this open environment. As the height increases, I can hear different sounds and see different scenery, which is exciting and refreshing!
Simple hand climbing is irresistible, allowing people to experience the beauty of scenery and architecture from all sides. Oh yeah!

Das Erklimmen von Gebäuden mit bloßen Händen ist eine spannende Herausforderung, denn man hält sich fest an die kalte Außenseite des Gebäudes, spürt ihren Herzschlag und ihre Atmung. Sein Blick war fest auf den hohen Boden gerichtet, wo das Ziel eine Herausforderung für sich selbst war.
Climbing building surfaces with bare hands is fraught with danger in reality, but this software does not have such danger relatively, and the immersive visual impact makes us more enjoyable.
Follow the footsteps of this software and walk into tower shaped buildings around the world, enjoying climbing with bare hands.
Climbing buildings around the world with bare hands without any danger was once my dream. I never thought this software would be so interesting, just like my dream.

I enjoy climbing, but I am afraid of danger and also require a certain economic foundation. But in this software, you can climb with bare hands without any danger, which is a major highlight of this software. I love it!
I love adventure, climbing and other games, but in reality, the cost of playing them is too high. This software perfectly realizes my dream of climbing!
Unlimited climbing of famous buildings around the world, where you can also enjoy the surrounding scenery, such as wind, bird sounds, waves, and more, without leaving your home.
This software is great. It does not affect work or normal life, and can still climb famous buildings around the world, with unlimited time and frequency.

After climbing to the top of the building, you can wander around, it's very exciting! At the beginning, I was a little afraid, which was much more terrible than walking on the glass walkway, because there was nothing below, and it was still so high from the ground.
非常糟糕的体验，bug多到离谱，无法转向，自动前进，没有物理碰撞各种穿模，为什么不修改一下？？？？
徒手攀爬知名建筑，瞬间游历世界各地，且不用出这个门票那个景点票的，这种感受简直不要太爽。
This climbing game is interesting and I really like it.
Climbing to the top of the building, you can activate the aerial roaming mode. Friends who are afraid of heights need to adapt and challenge their mentality.

I'm a bit afraid of heights. After climbing up the Eiffel Tower, I activated the high-altitude aerial roaming mode. I was so scared that I took off my helmet several times, but still couldn't resist the excitement. I put on my helmet again and continued playing the game.
Climbing high and looking far, one can also wander at high altitudes, which is simply exhilarating.
This climbing game is interesting. After climbing to the top of the building with bare hands, you can also start aerial roaming.
I like this climbing challenge game.
Climbing world-renowned buildings with bare hands, challenging time and time again, happy.
A game that I really like.
I like the feeling of this climbing challenge.

Vertigo-inducing yet somehow quite Zen. Has a good variety of stages. Enjoyable in its simplicity. Once one has got the hang of waiting for feedback from the gloves, it's possible to climb quite fast should one desire, or to go slowly and admire the scenery -- or even look downwards at the several hundred feet of sheer drop below. It runs well including on Linux.
A fun game!
En grimpant la Tour Eiffel, il est possible de se promener en hauteur, ce jeu est vraiment amusant.
Favorite games allow you to ascend for distant views or stroll through the air.
This game gives people a very unique experience, climbing tower shaped buildings around the world with bare hands, which is very fun and interesting.
喜欢的游戏，可登高远眺，可空中漫步。
The different sights actually look pretty cool for the budget price. Unfortunately, the climbing offers no challenge or depth to the gameplay.
A game in which you can climb famous structures, conquering them in turn. Acceptable graphics, atmospheric, sounds correspond to the locations. Sometimes there are small bugs, but overall it's fun
When the developers say "Extreme Climbing" they really mean it! EC is every virtual climber's dream because it lets you challenge otherwise unreachable heights and break down reality to the bone.
VR. Mountaineer simulator in which you can climb one of the famous buildings. The graphics are simple, but nevertheless there is an atmosphere and a sense of height. It's a good cardio game.
Unity, OpenVR. VR works out of the box on linux.
I recommend this game for VR in general. I will test it on Steam Frame as soon as I get my hands on one.
